what_happened: the spot lane pooled one finding across two rows: it named a gloss/splice extent mismatch at two different sites, one belonging to this row and one belonging to a different row. The docket builder attached the pooled finding to both rows. On this row the author found that half the cure named material the row does not contain anywhere in its 22 fields.
what_the_author_did: executed the half that belongs to this row and REFUSED the half that does not, on the ground that writing it would fabricate content the row does not carry. It reported the refusal with its reason instead of silently dropping it or inventing the material.
verification: the other half of the pooled finding names the same defect as a second finding already ordered on this row from a different lane, and that one was cured, so the row's actual defect is closed. The site belonging to the OTHER row is ordered separately on that row in the same docket.
why_this_is_right: the author law says a cure that cannot be executed truthfully is reported with its byte reason and the row still ships with every other cure. Fabricating a citation to satisfy an order is the failure mode this rule exists to prevent.
orchestrator_disposition: accepted as a correct refusal; no further order. The postcheck scope carries reported items by rule, so the final reviewer will re-test it independently.
process_lesson: a spot lane that pools one finding across two rows produces an order that is only half-executable on each. The docket builder should split a pooled finding per row at build time; recorded for the next book.
